answer: Each epoch the marble board auctions 100 slots; each applicant files a relic record for one past job. A bidder locks 50 copper as a bid bond plus its winning bid; auditors publish bids, so a duplicate relic cancels both slots and burns both bonds. The first slot clears at 20 copper and the hundredth at 500, since bids rise as slots fill, so each fake pays more than the last plus 50 copper. Taking 1,000 fakes needs ten epochs and 325,000 copper in bonds plus bids, while a rented relic fails because its hash already sits on the board. An honest agent bids once for 20 copper and keeps its slot.
